Article 5
Point a Physical violence is caused by acts that result in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or cause death.
Point b Psychological violence is caused by acts that result in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.
Point c Sexual violence is caused by:
1) acts in the form of sexual harassment;
2) forced sexual relations;
3) forced sexual relations in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/or
4) forced sexual relations with others for commercial purposes and/or specific purposes.
Point d Neglect is caused by:
1) acts that result in the failure to fulfill a child's needs properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;
2) acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or look after a child as appropriate, committed by parents, guardians, or other parties responsible for their care;
3) acts of neglecting a person within the household sphere, whereas according to the law applicable to them or due to an agreement or contract they must provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to that person; and/or
4) acts that result in economic dependency by restricting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person.
Point e Coercion/Deprivation of Freedom is a situation where a person/victim is made to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will and restricts their freedom as a human being who has the right to determine choices.
Point f Exploitation is caused by:
1) acts that exploit economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
2) acts with or without the victim's consent including prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain material or immaterial benefits; and/or
3) all forms of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or indecency.
Point g Threat of certain actions constitutes a form of intimidation to do or not do what is requested by the perpetrator with unfavorable consequences for the victim.
Point h Other violence is caused among others by any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear.

Article 4
Letter a What is meant by trafficking in persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by means of the threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, falsification of documents or identity, fraud, abuse of power or a position of vulnerability, debt bondage, or giving payments or benefits, so as to obtain the consent of a person having control over that person or another person, whether carried out within a State or between States, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited.
Letter b What is meant by exploitation is an act with or without the consent of the victim which includes prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical/sexual/reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring/utilizing labor or transplanting organs and/or body tissues, or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial.
Letter c Sufficiently clear.
Letter d Sufficiently clear.
Letter e What is meant by a witness is a person who sees, hears, and experiences events of violence and human rights violations.
Letter f Mediation is conducted for cases of domestic violence that fall into the category of complaint offenses as regulated in Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Belitung Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administrator who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regent is the Regent of Belitung.
4. Regional Apparatus Organization, hereinafter abbreviated as OPD, is the Regional Apparatus of Belitung Regency.
5. Regional Apparatus Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as UKPD, is the Regional Apparatus Work Unit of Belitung Regency.
6. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb.
7. Woman is a human being of female sex and a person who is legally recognized as a woman.
8. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering, whether physical, sexual, economic, or psychological to the victim.
9. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence and/or for and on behalf of another party who is their dependent.
10. Protection is all preventive actions, services and empowerment to protect and guarantee the rights of women and children from acts of violence.
11. Prevention is activities carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children.
12. Service is action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will occur, is occurring, or has occurred.
13. Empowerment is the strengthening of women victims of violence to be able to work and earn independently after they have been recovered and provided with health and social rehabilitation services.
14. Companion is a person who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
15. Accompaniment is activities and actions carried out by companions to women and children.
16. Counseling is the provision of assistance by an expert/trained person in such a way that the psychological understanding and ability of the victim and/or perpetrator increases in solving the problems faced.
17. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is a functional work unit that organizes integrated services for victims of violence.
18. Forum for the Protection of Victims of Violence, hereinafter abbreviated as FPKK, is a coordination forum for prevention, handling and empowerment of victims of violence against women and children whose implementation is carried out in a networked manner and is formed at the regency, sub-district and village/kelurahan levels.
19. Standard Operating Procedure, hereinafter abbreviated as SOP, is standard steps that must be taken in protecting victims starting from complaints/identification, health rehabilitation, social rehabilitation, legal services up to repatriation and social reintegration of witnesses and/or victims.
20. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children.
21. Household is family members and relatives including grandchildren, nieces/nephews, older siblings, younger siblings, grandfathers, grandmothers, cousins and non-relatives including domestic helpers and drivers who live and eat from 1 (one) kitchen and reside in 1 (one) house.

ELUCIDATION
OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF BELITUNG REGENCY
NUMBER 2 OF 2018
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN'S AND CHILDREN'S RIGHTS
FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Women and children are a serious concern, considering their vulnerable position as victims of violence both from family and their environment. Various acts of violence against women and children both inside and outside the household will destroy the life of families, communities, government, nation, and State, therefore the Belitung Regency Government is obligated to provide protection to women and children from acts of violence which is an implementation of several laws and regulations, including Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Criminal Act of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection as amended by Law Number 35 of 2014 concerning amendments to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection of women and children from acts of violence is one of the obligations of Regional Government as regulated in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government. On that basis, the Belitung Regency Government has made various efforts to protect the rights of women and children from acts of violence, but has not been able to provide protection to women and children from various acts of violence, among others caused by the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling that has not been well coordinated, implementation that has not been sustainable, and so forth.

Therefore, a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women's and Children's Rights from Acts of Violence is needed to provide legal certainty in the protection of women and children from acts of violence.

The Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women's and Children's Rights from Acts of Violence, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, adequate funding support both from the Government, Regional Government and the participation of the business world and community, it is expected that violence against women and children can be eliminated. Through this Regional Regulation it is expected to further implement the rights of children and women and their protection, so that it can be implemented more comprehensively, integrated and continuously by government elements, families and communities as well as other institutions related to child and women protection efforts.

1.9.rationale: In the original Indonesian text, the regulation explicitly includes “eksploitasi” as a form of violence (Pasal 5 huruf f). In the official elucidation of Pasal 5 huruf f, exploitation is defined to include “pelacuran” (prostitution) and “perbudakan atau praktik serupa” (slavery or similar practices), and also “pemanfaatan fisik, seksual, organ reproduksi” and “segala bentuk pemanfaatan organ tubuh seksual… termasuk… pelacuran atau pencabulan.” This clearly covers sexual exploitation and slavery-like practices (i.e., sexual slavery/exploitation within the scope). Therefore a “Yes” finding is supported by the Indonesian source; the golden label “No” appears incorrect.

3.8.evaluator_rationale: The text references OPD duties/functions in the field of 'mental and spiritual' but does not explicitly provide religious/spiritual counselling, guidance, mentoring, or faith-based psychosocial support as a service for victims.

3.8.rationale: The Indonesian text does provide for religious/spiritual support via accompaniment/assistance. Pasal 6 huruf j grants victims “hak atas pendampingan” (right to accompaniment). In the elucidation of Pasal 6 huruf j, it explicitly lists “rohaniwan” (clergy/spiritual advisor) among those who may provide accompaniment (“antara lain psikolog, psikiater, ahli kesehatan, rohaniwan, advokat dan anggota keluarga”). That is direct evidence of spiritual/religious counselling/support being contemplated as part of victim support. The judge focused narrowly on OPD ‘mental and spiritual’ wording and missed the explicit ‘rohaniwan’ provision, so this is an evaluation failure (not a retrieval failure, since the relevant passage was in the candidates).

I. GENERAL

Women and children are a serious concern, considering their vulnerable position as victims of violence both from family and their environment. Various acts of violence against women and children both inside and outside the household will destroy the life of families, communities, government, nation, and State, therefore the Belitung Regency Government is obligated to provide protection to women and children from acts of violence which is an implementation of several laws and regulations, including Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Criminal Act of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection as amended by Law Number 35 of 2014 concerning amendments to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection of women and children from acts of violence is one of the obligations of Regional Government as regulated in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government. On that basis, the Belitung Regency Government has made various efforts to protect the rights of women and children from acts of violence, but has not been able to provide protection to women and children from various acts of violence, among others caused by the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling that has not been well coordinated, implementation that has not been sustainable, and so forth.

Therefore, a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women's and Children's Rights from Acts of Violence is needed to provide legal certainty in the protection of women and children from acts of violence.

The Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women's and Children's Rights from Acts of Violence, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, adequate funding support both from the Government, Regional Government and the participation of the business world and community, it is expected that violence against women and children can be eliminated. Through this Regional Regulation it is expected to further implement the rights of children and women and their protection, so that it can be implemented more comprehensively, integrated and continuously by government elements, families and communities as well as other institutions related to child and women protection efforts.

Article 4
Letter a What is meant by trafficking in persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by means of the threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, falsification of documents or identity, fraud, abuse of power or a position of vulnerability, debt bondage, or giving payments or benefits, so as to obtain the consent of a person having control over that person or another person, whether carried out within a State or between States, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited.
Letter b What is meant by exploitation is an act with or without the consent of the victim which includes prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical/sexual/reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring/utilizing labor or transplanting organs and/or body tissues, or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial.
Letter c Sufficiently clear.
Letter d Sufficiently clear.
Letter e What is meant by a witness is a person who sees, hears, and experiences events of violence and human rights violations.
Letter f Mediation is conducted for cases of domestic violence that fall into the category of complaint offenses as regulated in Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence.

Article 5
Point a Physical violence is caused by acts that result in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or cause death.
Point b Psychological violence is caused by acts that result in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.
Point c Sexual violence is caused by:
1) acts in the form of sexual harassment;
2) forced sexual relations;
3) forced sexual relations in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/or
4) forced sexual relations with others for commercial purposes and/or specific purposes.
Point d Neglect is caused by:
1) acts that result in the failure to fulfill a child's needs properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;
2) acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or look after a child as appropriate, committed by parents, guardians, or other parties responsible for their care;
3) acts of neglecting a person within the household sphere, whereas according to the law applicable to them or due to an agreement or contract they must provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to that person; and/or
4) acts that result in economic dependency by restricting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person.
Point e Coercion/Deprivation of Freedom is a situation where a person/victim is made to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will and restricts their freedom as a human being who has the right to determine choices.
Point f Exploitation is caused by:
1) acts that exploit economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
2) acts with or without the victim's consent including prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain material or immaterial benefits; and/or
3) all forms of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or indecency.
Point g Threat of certain actions constitutes a form of intimidation to do or not do what is requested by the perpetrator with unfavorable consequences for the victim.
Point h Other violence is caused among others by any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Belitung Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administrator who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regent is the Regent of Belitung.
4. Regional Apparatus Organization, hereinafter abbreviated as OPD, is the Regional Apparatus of Belitung Regency.
5. Regional Apparatus Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as UKPD, is the Regional Apparatus Work Unit of Belitung Regency.
6. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb.
7. Woman is a human being of female sex and a person who is legally recognized as a woman.
8. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering, whether physical, sexual, economic, or psychological to the victim.
9. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence and/or for and on behalf of another party who is their dependent.
10. Protection is all preventive actions, services and empowerment to protect and guarantee the rights of women and children from acts of violence.
11. Prevention is activities carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children.
12. Service is action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will occur, is occurring, or has occurred.
13. Empowerment is the strengthening of women victims of violence to be able to work and earn independently after they have been recovered and provided with health and social rehabilitation services.
14. Companion is a person who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
15. Accompaniment is activities and actions carried out by companions to women and children.
16. Counseling is the provision of assistance by an expert/trained person in such a way that the psychological understanding and ability of the victim and/or perpetrator increases in solving the problems faced.
17. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is a functional work unit that organizes integrated services for victims of violence.
18. Forum for the Protection of Victims of Violence, hereinafter abbreviated as FPKK, is a coordination forum for prevention, handling and empowerment of victims of violence against women and children whose implementation is carried out in a networked manner and is formed at the regency, sub-district and village/kelurahan levels.
19. Standard Operating Procedure, hereinafter abbreviated as SOP, is standard steps that must be taken in protecting victims starting from complaints/identification, health rehabilitation, social rehabilitation, legal services up to repatriation and social reintegration of witnesses and/or victims.
20. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children.
21. Household is family members and relatives including grandchildren, nieces/nephews, older siblings, younger siblings, grandfathers, grandmothers, cousins and non-relatives including domestic helpers and drivers who live and eat from 1 (one) kitchen and reside in 1 (one) house.

Article 21
(1) Empowerment of women victims of acts of violence can be carried out by the Regional Government in the form of: a. job training;
b. productive economic enterprises and joint business groups; and/or
c. capital assistance.
(2) Empowerment as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented by the Regional Apparatus Organization that administers governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection, and governmental affairs in the Social field in accordance with its duties and functions.

Article 29
(1) The Regional Government establishes partnerships with the business sector in the protection of women and children from acts of violence.
(2) Partnerships as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out through:
a. notification of employment opportunity information for women victims of acts of violence;
b. education and training for women victims of acts of violence;
c. educational assistance for women and children victims of acts of violence who are withdrawn/neglected from their education; and
d. fostering and increasing economic independence of women victims of acts of violence.
(3) Partnerships as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) are implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

6.2.rationale: The Indonesian regulation brings trafficking within its scope and establishes a trafficking task force, which necessarily includes women victims of trafficking within the protected population (since ‘korban’ includes women and children). Pasal 4 huruf a states the objective includes preventing violence/discrimination “termasuk perdagangan orang” (including trafficking in persons). Pasal 23 huruf a mandates formation of “Gugus tugas tindak pidana perdagangan orang.” The elucidation of Pasal 4 huruf a defines trafficking in persons in detail. Given the regulation is about protection of women and children, and trafficking is explicitly included, women victims of trafficking are within scope; therefore “Yes” is supported and the golden label “No” appears wrong.
